newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-BJORKMAN LATEST SEED TO FALL AT AT&T CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BJORKMAN LATEST SEED TO FALL AT AT&T CHALLENGE.

text.p: Second-seeded Jonas Bjorkman of Sweden became the latest favourite to fall at the $328,000 AT&T Challenge when he was eliminated in the second round by Australian Sandon Stolle on Wednesday.

Bjorkman's loss sapped the tournament of all three of its top seeds. Michael Chang, seeded first, and third-seeded Jim Courier both lost Tuesday. Bjorkman's exit left fourth-seeded Andre Agassi as the only major name remaining in the field.
Sixth-seeded American Alex O'Brien was given a clay court lesson by Uruguay's Marcelo Filippini, with Filippini advancing 7-6 (8-6) 6-4 in another upset decision.
American Chris Woodruff, the eighth seed, was the only surviving seed on Wednesday. Woodruff beat Argentina's Javier Frana 7-6 (7-2) 6-2.
Stolle, son of former Australian Davis Cup player Fred Stolle, took advantage of Bjorkman's failure to put away the match in the second set after the 22nd-ranked Swede won the first set 6-4.
Stolle missed his first set point at 5-4 in the second set but clinched finished off a 7-2 tiebreaker with an ace.
The Australian got a break in the opening game of the third set and again at 5-2 and rolled to an easy 6-2 win.

Stolle, ranked 68, has enjoyed great success in doubles, winning six titles, but has yet to win a title in singles. He competed in his first Davis Cup tie for Australia earlier this year, defeating Cedric Pioline of France in a dead rubber. His appearance marked the first time a father and son had both competed in Davis Cup for Australia.
"The Davis Cup experience was big, especially as I had a win," Stolle said. "It was pretty exciting."
Stolle said he felt comfortable against Bjorkman having beaten the Swede on three previous occasions.
"I never lost to him and I match up well with him," Stolle said. "I knew if I hung in and played my game I'm capable of beating him. Towards the end I really played well and he got frustrated."
Bjorkman said his losing record with Stolle played on his mind.
"It's a little frustrating," Bjorkman said. "Every single time he plays me he plays well. I see him losing to other players really badly and every time I play him he's coming up with great tennis."
Filippini honed his skills at tournaments in Barcelona, Estoril and Orlando before coming to Atlanta and the experience showed.
"I am playing some good tennis the last four weeks," he said. "I am getting more comfortable and more confident on the court."
